reason: The text depicts Jacob responding to Laban's accusations with anger and vigorous defense rather than humility. When Laban confronts Jacob, stating 'What have you done? You've stolen my heart and led away my daughters like captives' (וַיִּ֥חַר לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיָּ֣רֶב בְּלָבָ֑ן - Jacob becomes angry and contends with Laban). Jacob then launches into a lengthy 20-year account detailing his own faithfulness and labor, defending his virtue and highlighting Laban's failures, rather than humbly accepting criticism. The text presents Jacob's leadership model through his hard work, diligence, and resourcefulness, but explicitly demonstrates a confrontational rather than humble response to criticism.
